3D Heat Transfer

GPU volume rendering of a diffusing heat pulse in 3D.

3D Heat Transfer Volume (GPU)
Temperature-dependent properties (k, cp, rho, eps) are sampled from tables (T in K). Preset tables are approximate; replace with your own measurements for high precision.
Using built-in k(T) and cp(T) tables for Aluminum.

Uses a 3D heat diffusion kernel with an optional lumped convection decay term to reflect heat loss to the ambient.
Radiation is linearized around the ambient temperature (using h_rad=4*epsilon*sigma*T_inf^3). Toggle "temps in C" off if you enter Kelvin directly.
Point/patch heat sources are modeled as Gaussian blobs that diffuse over time (additional terms in the field).
Anisotropic diffusion uses independent alpha_x, alpha_y, alpha_z with separate Gaussian widths.
